verdict.rationale: The evidence only implies hardware abstraction. Isaac validates robot stacks through ROS 2 and a ROS bridge, and supports software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop testing of the same perception and mobility stacks, so application code is decoupled from the backing hardware (simulated or real). Isaac ROS also offers plug-and-play packages, and users can add their own robots and physics-based sensors. None of this explicitly documents stable sensor/actuator abstraction interfaces or hot-swapping hardware without code changes. Missing for 10: explicit hardware-abstraction/driver interface documentation, evidence of swapping physical sensors or actuators without app rewrites, and independent hands-on corroboration.
